item.text:
**Bottom Line**
Weaker than inherited, or at best flat on a very low baseline. 2024 produced a few procedural and inclusion wins, but the dominant pattern was continued repression, weak accountability, a disputed legitimacy environment, and an October term-limit/third-term entrenchment push. I found no credible evidence of a broad net strengthening of political freedom or democratic resilience.

**Accepted Claims**
- [Freedom in the World 2025: Democratic Republic of the Congo](https://freedomhouse.org/country/democratic-republic-congo/freedom-world/2025) | Freedom House | 2025 | Freedom House still rated the DRC “Not Free” and said citizens were increasingly unable to exercise basic civil liberties; the report’s 2024 section frames Tshisekedi’s second term as beginning after a flawed election and worsening political conditions. | 4B.10, 4B.1, 4B.3, 4B.6, 4B.7, 4B.9

- [World Report 2025: Democratic Republic of Congo](https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2025/country-chapters/democratic-republic-congo) | Human Rights Watch | 2025 | HRW says authorities cracked down on opposition members, civil society activists, critics, and journalists throughout 2024, used arrests and prosecutions against critics, and kept civic and media space under heavy pressure. That points to a weaker democratic environment by year-end than at the start of the year. | 4B.10, 4B.3, 4B.6, 4B.7, 4B.9

- [2024 Country Reports on Human Rights Practices: Democratic Republic of the Congo](https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2128488.html) | U.S. Department of State | 2024 | The report says there were no significant improvements in the human-rights situation, lists serious restrictions on expression and media freedom, and says the government made only limited progress on holding abusers accountable. This is strong evidence against any claim that 2024 strengthened democratic resilience. | 4B.10, 4B.3, 4B.6, 4B.7, 4B.9

- [DRC: President Tshisekedi must use second term to tackle human rights crisis](https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/06/drc-president-tshisekedi-must-use-second-term-to-tackle-human-rights-crisis/) | Amnesty International | 2024-06-24 | Amnesty said Tshisekedi’s first term produced little to no progress on human rights and that the country entered the second term with shrinking civic space and worsening armed conflict. That is direct evidence that the inheritance was not improved in a meaningful way by mid-2024. | 4B.10, 4B.3, 4B.6, 4B.7, 4B.9

- [Congo president Tshisekedi draws criticism over constitutional reform plans](https://www.yahoo.com/news/congo-president-tshisekedi-draws-criticism-154945419.html) | Reuters | 2024-10-24 | Tshisekedi’s constitutional-reform push raised fears that term limits could be removed and a third term enabled. This is one of the clearest 2024 signals that democratic resilience was being weakened rather than strengthened. | 4B.10, 4B.1, 4B.8, 4B.3

- [DR Congo appoints country's first female prime minister](https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/dr-congo-president-appoints-countrys-first-female-prime-minister-2024-04-01/) | Reuters | 2024-04-01 | Tshisekedi appointed Judith Suminwa Tuluka as the country’s first female prime minister, a real but limited inclusion gain. It improved symbolic representation, but it did not offset the broader repression and institutional fragility. | 4B.10, 4B.7, 4B.8

- [DR Congo names new government after months of delay](https://www.marketscreener.com/news/latest/DR-Congo-names-new-government-after-months-of-delay-46846207/) | Reuters | 2024-05-29 | The new government was finally formed after prolonged coalition bargaining, which shows some willingness to work through parliamentary coalition procedures instead of bypassing them entirely. This is positive, but procedural and narrow. | 4B.10, 4B.8, 4B.1

- [Les Téké et les Yaka s’engagent à mettre fin aux hostilités dans l’ouest de la Rdc](https://www.presidence.cd/actualite-detail/actualite/les_teke_et_les_yaka_sengagent_a_mettre_fin_aux_hostilites_dans_louest_de_la_rdc) | Présidence RDC | 2024-04-06 | Tshisekedi presided over a local peace agreement between Téké and Yaka representatives, with dialogue and arbitration commitments. This is a limited positive signal for conflict de-escalation and community reconciliation, not a broad democratic restoration. | 4B.10, 4B.7, 4B.6

- [Congolese president Tshisekedi sworn in for second term after disputed vote](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/congolese-president-tshisekedi-sworn-in-for-second-term-after-disputed-vote-3278886) | Reuters | 2024-01-20 | Tshisekedi entered 2024 under a cloud of disputed legitimacy, with opponents refusing to recognize the result because of widespread irregularities. That weak starting point matters for the 4B.10 comparison and makes a net democratic improvement harder to sustain. | 4B.10, 4B.1, 4B.8

**Search Gap**
I found no strong evidence that 2024 produced a durable, system-wide strengthening of political freedom or democratic resilience. The positive evidence was real but narrow: one female PM, coalition bargaining, and a few localized de-escalation steps. The stronger evidence points to continued repression, institutional distrust, and an apparent move toward entrenchment.
